item.title: Re: Lantern Jack
item.content:encoded:
Your idea is very vague, yet I will review it

+ Click for review
- Bing Bong, Im a collapsible

Your Pitch: You have to specify what the twist is to Stingy Jack, because if not its like saying, "The SCP has anomalous effects". You need to summarize the twist in the pitch.

The Narrative: The SCP moves around with unknown means? As if no one has ever saw it walk, fly, teleport, etc? You can't just say it moves around with unknown means, as that would be really hard to know an SCP exist and not know how it moves! He takes items from the SCP foundation, so I can infer he usually rudimentary ways of moving, such as walking, running, swimming, etc., But how the hell can he take items from the Foundation if he's in a containment cell?
SCP-XXXX uses the Foundations own words against itself? The Stinging Jack story shows the Devil making a Deal with Jack, but you see, Jack has basic rights, SCPs do not. If the SCP Foundation said, "Hey come here, we won't contain you, we promise" and then contained you, there is no way you can fight that, as again, SCPs do not have basic rights, its a prison, not a hotel.

The Hook: I will not comment on this as it does not seem relevant to this SCP.

Basically, just specify more of this SCP, and message me, I will do a more formal review.

item.title: Re: [Seeking Greenlights] The Ambassador's Strolling Players
item.content:encoded:
So my biggest problem with this is that other than an "otherworldly playhouse" this doesn't feel particularly connected to Alagadda lore. Which makes me wonder why its connected at all?

+ show block
– hide block

I think you need to up the weirdness. Read The Hanged King's play SCP and the Alagadda SCP by Metaphysician, and try to capture some of that surreal flavor. Either that or completely withdraw this story from that lore and make it your own.

I don't want to be "that guy" but this feels more like a tale, in the way you've laid it out. What is the anomaly that the Article will be centered around?

Also… keep in mind, the Hanged King's play tends to be very bad for the audience… and yet we have lots and lots of researchers going for it without much in the way of consequences.

Finally:

He hands the doctor a packet filled with containment procedures for some of the Foundation's most nasty SCPs.

Wouldn't the Foundation already have these? Why is this valuable enough for the Researchers to risk themselves by going through this procedure?

Overall: this feels like a sorta shallow attempt to hook into the Alagadda lore, but without the madness and frightening alien horrors.

Central Narrative: The Central Narrative revolves around SCP-XXXX-1 mostly, who absorbs Conscious entities and their knowledge, the process usually takes a couple of hours before it fully will becomes one with the entity. If you are 4.3km2 near the Vicinity of SCP-XXXX, SCP-XXXX-1 may rarely attempt to communicate psychically to a person. item.title: Re: Night Terrors - Seeking Idea Critique
item.content:encoded:
I have a good idea of what this SCP is, and what she can do, but I need a bit of help figuring out the specifics of her story.

See, the anomaly isn't that interesting. I feel like there's a lot of "little kids that are dangerous without knowing it" on the wiki and in fiction entirely… But what could set you apart is the story. How you characterize the child, the researchers, and how you create an emotional arc (or journey) for the reader to go on.

Honestly, no one is going to be able to help you write this, its something you have to answer for yourself.

Ask yourself the following questions, and then try to answer them by editing the post to reflect your feelings on the answers:

  • Who's perspective is the article from? Who are we going to relate to as readers?
  • Where are the stakes for this narrative? Beyond the fact that there are monsters… what is the intrigue? Only figuring out what is going on with the girl? Is there some way you could up the drama/stakes?
  • What sort of tone are you going for? Is this scary? Is this an emotional story?

Mostly suggest you stay away from vivid descriptions of the abuse the child goes through, unless its super important to the narrative. Shock value is a weak story aspect.

item.title: A statue that moves through the darkness (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch:

  • An SCP that can disrupt electricity
  • An SCP that can only move around when light doesn't touch the SCP

Central Narrative: This SCP is a stone statue that dates from during the renaissance age. The stone statue is broken having no right elbow, no nose, and a broken hilt. The reason for this is probably old age.

The foundation went under investigation after a group of archeologists went missing somewhere in France. When the foundation located the SCP they found it inside a cave, the cave was decorated with marble columns, and torches were lit inside it. All electrical devices and electrical lights got disrupted and the foundation took the SCP within it, however, since the foundation found the SCP in the middle of the night 10 personnel were later killed trying to transport the statue. After the incident, the foundation decided to transport the SCP in a small container lit by the torches that were within the cave.

The foundation needs to use non-electrical light producers meaning they can't use lightbulbs, spotlights, flashlights to stop the SCP from moving and killing everyone. Only visible light can stop the SCP from moving such as sunlight, candlelight, and etc. The reason why this SCP can't move under light is unknown but there are two current theories.

The statue hasn't been in a brighter light other than the torches for a very long time.
The statue was made from a human, the statue's purpose is to be in the spotlight, to entertain and amaze humans. It's not supposed to move because that is not what they are supposed to do, only in the dark they are allowed to move.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP can disrupt electricity which renders light bulbs, flashlights, phones, and even clean energy useless. This makes the SCP harder to contain when light bulbs and spotlights aren't used against the SCP since lights immobilize the object. So the foundation has to use oil lamps, candles, and torches to keep the SCP from breach containment.

Additional Notes: I seek feedbacks and criticisms, thank you.

item.title: Re: Infinity war but in SCP
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Bawower, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor offical reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
Wooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So your pitch is some kind of collaboration between all of the major GoIs to stop… something, however tensions arise due to everyone being suspicious of everyone else? At the moment, this seems more like a Tale than an SCP. It it's also ambitious. Very ambitious. This kind of thing would require an immense amount of research and the like to pull off, and I don't know if a new author such as yourself would be skilled enough to execute this effectively. You're also quite vague about what the GoIs are fighting against. What is it?

Central Narrative

An unknown individual that is notably immature sends a threat message to every GoI, and despite having absolutely no evidence whatsoever to back up their claims, every GoI believes them and unites? This, to a relatively knowledgeable member of the Site (which they probably would be, if, hypothetically, they were reading this) would be an immediate shattering of the suspension of disbelief. This simply isn't feasible. You need to come up with a more pressing threat if you want to make this idea reasonable.

Hook/Attention Grabber

That the SCP will unite all of the GoIs, that's a good hook. The next part, which features gratuitous name-dropping of pop culture references (specifically Among Us), isn't. Try to keep away from that if possible.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I don't know about this, buddy

This idea has the potential to work well, but there are some crippling problems. Firstly, this seems more like a Tale than an SCP (but it could still work as an SCP), due to your vagueness on what the anomaly actually is, and much more of the focus on the 'GoI unification' part. Secondly, your vagueness on the anomaly is really shooting you in the foot here. As I have no idea what the anomaly behind this (and thus the whole point of the article) is, I can't really crit it. What I did see I wasn't impressed by due to logistical problems (see above section for detail). Thirdly, if this is based around Avengers: Infinity War (a mediocre movie, in my opinion), then why write about it if we've already seen it? Wouldn't that be plagiarism and/or boring?
To sum up, I personally don't like this idea due to it being incomplete (what is the anomaly?) and how it is unoriginal (a collaboration between all of the GoIs, if based on Infinity War, isn't original).

I'd recommend two things:
1. Checking out the Guide Hub (and more specifically this article, first section) for a whole bunch of great essays full of helpful advice!
2. Reaching out to some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad. They're really helpful and have tonnes of experience!

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence1:
A mysterious individual contacts every GoI and threatens them with an anomalous object capable of mass destruction, causing the all of the GoIs to unite to find and fight against the individual.

Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get a simple summary of the bare bones of your idea that a critter will see. You may find something here that you don't actually like, or find us critters are getting the wrong impression.

item.title: Time Traveling Ice Dispenser
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX represents a an extremely damaged and worn down ice dispensing machine. It was originally discovered by a team of Paleontologists on a expedition within the Bone Valley Formation, Florida, United States in 2018. From here it was reported in scientific literature, and was then taken to the foundation. From here it was kept within a anomalous item storage locker until SCP-XXXX began excreting a dark blue gas from its front.

Central Narrative: This gas designated SCP-XXXX-1 is not immediately dangerous, however once this gas is mixed with Oxygen, it will begin turning the surrounding air cold. Small doses of SCP-XXXX-1 is not harmful however large doses make the surrounding area extremely cold and as a consequence can cause frostbite as well as hyperthermia. Because of SCP-XXXX-1 the foundation wanted to look in the exterior of SCP-XXXX to see how it was producing SCP-XXXX-1 on an almost infinite level. However when looking inside of SCP-XXXX they discovered a small metal box witch contained two written notes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These notes were signed by Dr. [INSERT NAME HERE] as well having the dates on them, which were months ahead of the current date. The first of these was a copy of an updated page of SCP-XXXX with a stick it note saying "Might come in handy". The second is a warning stating how the author of the note Dr. [INSERT NAME HERE] is concerned about the foundation accessing the core of SCP-XXXX due to the possibility that SCP-XXXX-1 could flow infinitely out of SCP-XXXX leaving the audience on a cliffhanger.

Additional Notes:So the first part of the page will just be the usual Special containment procedures, description as well as an added discovery page. Next will be a warning stating only level 4 and over clearance is needed to access, once readers access they will learn about how it was originally kept in a items locker, SCP-XXXX-1 as well as the notes.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

Yes, there were folks in that brave era
Who had the hearts and souls of heroes:
Real men, unlike you lads!
They battled, but their luck turned ill, and
So many brave young men were killed then.
But Moscow, if God had not willed it,
Would never have changed hands!

Mikhail Lermontov, Borodino

Connecting some dots, introducing some new characters. Can't have a multi-pronged MTF without new members.

Thank you to Pedagon and as always, HarryBlank for their critique and help making this sing.

item.title: Get More Kanbans
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
This SCP is a yellow Post-It Note brand sticky note with the words "Get More Kanbans" written on it with black marker. Whenever someone reads the note, they will be sent into a trance state and will seek out sticky notes, write "Get More Kanbans" upon them, and then stick said notes around the SCP to create a kanban board. As the kanban board increases in size, those under its trance will become desperate, breaking into homes and supply stores to acquire notes to add to the board. If the subject is unable to acquire more notes, they will attempt to create sticky notes out of things such as paper, tape, cloth, or even their own earwax. There has been no found way to stop this trance, and as subjects will never stop trying to add to the board, they will often perish from starvation or physical exertion. When left without a tranced subject for too long, the SCP is able to manifest these notes in the surrounding area at a slow rate (which unlike the placed notes, have the trancing ability).

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
Several reports of small midwestern town citizens breaking into and stealing office supplies from the town over come out. The Foundation decides to investigate once several residents - including an officer - are arrested, having said to act manic in the holding cell before curling up onto the floor crying, refusing to eat, and subsequently dying from starvation/dehydration. The Foundation finds the SCP located in the basement of a house - the inside of the house covered in head to toe in sticky notes. After being contained, it is learned the SCP is able to manifest these notes on the opposite side of any wall it's placed on, managing to break containment for a moment, trancing a scientist. A few reports of supply store break-ins are reported again, and several notes are found to have manifested inside the house. Acquiring chunk of the drywall to examine it, millions of notes are found within the walls.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
That relatable feeling of stress when you are overwhelmed with work on a whole new level. As well as the humor of being obsessed with office supplies.

Additional Notes:
Not sentient.
While not fully explored, perhaps this SCP is fungus-like? Explaining its ability to "grow", and rather than having infectious spores you breath in, you "look them in"(?)

It should be mentioned: I do indeed have a rough draft for this SCP of which I started about a year ago before dropping it for awhile. Everything up until the addendums could pass as being completed, whereas the addendums themselves are only summaries of what I am hoping to write. The original idea was for this SCP to be "BUY More Kanbans" rather than "GET", and as such my current photo in the draft reflects such. Along with this, I do not have anything relating to the fungus idea mentioned prior - yet.

item.title: Re: Seeking out more greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch:

  • An SCP that can disrupt electricity
  • An SCP that can only move around when light doesn't touch the SCP

Central Narrative: This SCP is a stone statue that dates from during the renaissance age. The stone statue is broken having no right elbow, no nose, and a broken hilt. The reason for this is because the creator wanted to destroy what he/she created but couldn't find a way, so the creator stored it away in a cave.

+ show block
– hide block

The foundation went under investigation after a group of archeologists went missing somewhere in France. When the foundation located the SCP they found it inside a cave, the cave was decorated with marble columns, and torches were lit inside it. All electrical devices and electrical lights got disrupted and the foundation took the SCP within it, however, since the foundation found the SCP in the middle of the night 10 personnel were later killed trying to transport the statue. After the incident, the foundation decided to transport the SCP in a small container lit by the torches that were within the cave.

The foundation needs to use non-electrical light producers meaning they can't use lightbulbs, spotlights, flashlights to stop the SCP from moving and killing everyone. Only visible light can stop the SCP from moving such as sunlight, candlelight, and etc. The reason why this SCP can't move under light is unknown but there are two current theories.

  1. The statue hasn't been in a brighter light other than the torches for a very long time.
  2. The statue was made from a human, the statue's purpose is to be in the spotlight, to entertain and amaze humans. It's not supposed to move because that is not what they are supposed to do, only in the dark they are allowed to move.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP can disrupt electricity which renders light bulbs, flashlights, phones, and even clean energy useless. This makes the SCP harder to contain when light bulbs and spotlights aren't used against the SCP since lights immobilize the object. So the foundation has to use oil lamps, candles, and torches to keep the SCP from breach containment.

Additional Notes: I have redone parts in this greenlight, I would love to see some feedback or criticism from experienced writers.
